newsitem.title: UK: WPP buys stake in U.S.-based HyperParallel.
newsitem.headline: WPP buys stake in U.S.-based HyperParallel.

text.p: WPP Group Plc, the advertising and marketing group, on Monday said it has taken a stake in a San Francisco-based company that helps firms make use of consumer data.
The purchase of the stake in San Francisco-based HyperParallel brings to seven WPP's investments in new media companies. WPP said the acquisition complements its direct marketing activities.

Founded in 1995, HyperParallel is a so-called data mining company, which helps companies use their transactional data to better understand consumer behaviour and the impact of price, brand name and merchandising mix on brand loyalty and spending.

HyperParallel's clients include Bank of America, Wal-Mart, Caldor and Telstra. WPP said its direct-marketing businesses and HyperParallel have already been working in partnership on various client projects.

"The industry is at an early stage," Eric Salama, director of strategy for WPP, said in a statement. "Working with HP will help us introduce leading-edge technology and thinking into our clients and will complement the direct marketing capabilities we already have within the group."
WPP's other investments in new media companies include ventures in Internet publishing and Internet direct marketing, on-line shopping, and World Wide Web development.
